subject: general
question: Which of the following movements created regional disparities between large and small farmers in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Green revolution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution refers to the set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives occurring between the 1940s and the late 1960s that increased agricultural production worldwide, especially in developing countries.
 
• In India, the Green Revolution was launched in the 1960s with the introduction of high-yielding varieties (HYVs) of seeds, increased use of fertilizers, and improved irrigation methods to boost food production.
 
• The Green Revolution led to a significant increase in food grain production, particularly wheat and rice, transforming India from a food-deficient country to one of the world's leading agricultural nations.
 
• However, the benefits of the Green Revolution were not evenly distributed, creating regional disparities and widening the gap between large and small farmers, as well as between different regions of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yellow Revolution:**

 
 
• The Yellow Revolution refers to the increase in the production of oilseeds in India, especially mustard and sunflower, initiated in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
 
• It aimed at achieving self-sufficiency in edible oil production to reduce dependence on imports.
 
 
 
• **Pink Revolution:**
 
 
• The Pink Revolution refers to the technological advancement and growth in the production of meat and poultry in India.
 
• It focuses on improving the quality and quantity of meat production, especially in the poultry sector.
 
 
 
• **Blue Revolution:**
 
 
• The Blue Revolution refers to the rapid increase in fish production and aquaculture in India.
 
• It aims to enhance the productivity of fisheries and aquaculture through sustainable practices and technological advancements.
